mainTopic: When a flawed blood service creates שירים, and when blood becomes דחוי
overview: The amud opens by closing an earlier discussion: a ברייתא refutes ריש לקיש. The גמרא then asks when a flawed blood service turns the rest of the blood into שירים. רבי יוחנן says only a service done with intent for outside its time or place does this, because only such a service can make the offering פיגול. Three versions of the question follow. One asks about an unfit person, one asks about a cup of disqualified blood, and one asks about an unused valid cup, which ties into a dispute between the רבנן and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. Next, the גמרא explains why the משנה needs three cases: an unfit person, the left hand, and a non-sacred vessel. It then asks why the blood is not דחוי in these cases. רבינא says the משנה follows חנן המצרי, who holds there is no דחוי. רב אשי says anything a person can fix himself is not דחוי, and רב שייא backs רב אשי from רבי יהודה's own rulings. The amud ends with the חכמים challenging רבי יהודה's ruling about sprinkling a cup of mixed blood, and his reply continues on the next amud.

steps.title: ריש לקיש's view is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with the word 'disqualified', and the גמרא declares that this is a conclusive refutation of ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...and it is disqualified. This is a refutation of ריש לקיש! Yes, it is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא from the previous discussion and declares that it disproves ריש לקיש's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ופסול' is the last word of the ברייתא that was being quoted. The ברייתא's ruling contradicts what ריש לקיש said. The גמרא gives no answer for him, so his view is rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation; a source that disproves an opinion
'A refutation of so-and-so': the formula for raising a strong challenge

steps.whatToRemember: When the גמרא repeats 'תיובתא' alone after 'תיובתא ד...', it means the opinion is fully rejected, with no answer offered.

phrases.english: and it is disqualified.
phrases.notes: This is the last word of the ברייתא quoted at the end of the previous discussion.

phrases.english: This is a refutation of Reish Lakish!
It is indeed a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion from the previous part of the daf.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ריש לקיש's opinion is refuted by the ברייתא and is rejected.

steps.title: Does an unfit person's service turn the rest of the blood into leftovers?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about collecting blood with a wrong intent. ריש לקיש asks רבי יוחנן whether a פסול who did the blood service makes the rest of the blood שירים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And all of them that collected...' ריש לקיש asked רבי יוחנן: If an unfit person did the blood service, does that make the remaining blood into leftovers?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the משנה, and ריש לקיש asks a clarifying question about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that after a service done with מחשבת חוץ לזמנו or חוץ למקומו, a fit כהן may collect again if דם הנפש is still left in the animal. ריש לקיש wants to know about a different bad service: one done by a פסול. Does his act 'use up' the blood, so that what remains is only שירים? Or does his act count for nothing, so a fit כהן can still do the service properly?

keyTerms.meaning: 'And all of them that collected': the opening words of the משנה being discussed
He asked of him
Here: a person who is unfit for Temple service
What is the law?
Leftover blood, which can no longer be used for the main blood service

steps.confusionAlert: שירים does not mean the blood is thrown away. It means the remaining blood can no longer be used for the main, essential service, because that service has already been 'done', even if it was done badly.

phrases.english: And all of them that collected, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה about collecting blood with intent for outside its time or place. כו׳ means 'and so on'.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish asked Rabbi Yoḥanan:
An unfit person: what is the law, does he render the remaining blood leftovers?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion on the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a service done by a פסול count enough to turn the remaining blood into שירים?

steps.title: Only time or place intent creates leftovers
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that only a service done with intent for outside its time or outside its place creates שירים, because that service counts enough to make the offering פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Nothing creates leftovers except a service done with intent for outside its time or outside its place, since that service 'works' to make the offering פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers no: a פסול's service does not make the remaining blood שירים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A service done with מחשבת חוץ לזמנו is strong enough to make the offering פיגול, so the Torah treats it as a real, completed service. That is why it uses up the blood. A פסול's service has no such power, so it counts for nothing, and a fit כהן may still do the service with the remaining blood.

keyTerms.meaning: Intent to eat or offer the sacrifice after its proper time
Intent to eat or offer the sacrifice outside its proper place
Since; because
Effects acceptance; counts as a valid service
An offering made forbidden by intent to eat it after its proper time

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, a bad service creates שירים only if it is 'valid enough' to cause פיגול. A פסול's service is not, so the remaining blood can still be used.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Nothing renders the blood leftovers
except intent for beyond its time and outside its place,
since it effects acceptance with regard to making it piggul.
phrases.notes: He means that this service counts as 'done' enough to make the offering פיגול, so it really uses up the blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֵין עוֹשֶׂה שִׁירַיִם אֶלָּא חוּץ לִזְמַנּוֹ וְחוּץ לִמְקוֹמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ריש לקיש's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A פסול does not create שירים. Only מחשבת חוץ לזמנו or חוץ למקומו does, since that service counts enough to create פיגול.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a principle: whether a flawed service 'uses up' the blood depends on whether that service has any legal standing.

steps.title: רב זביד's version: the question was about a disqualified cup
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד reports the exchange differently: ריש לקיש asked whether a כוס פסול (a cup of disqualified blood) creates שירים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד teaches it this way: ריש לקיש asked רבי יוחנן: If a cup of disqualified blood was offered, does it make the remaining blood into leftovers?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the conversation, in which ריש לקיש's question is about a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version the problem is not the person doing the service but the blood itself. The cup of blood became disqualified, for example by leaving the Temple courtyard, and was then offered anyway. The question is whether that offering uses up the remaining blood in the animal.

keyTerms.meaning: Teaches it this way: introduces another version
A cup of disqualified blood

phrases.english: Rav Zevid teaches it this way:

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish asked Rabbi Yoḥanan:
A disqualified cup: what is the law, does it render the remaining blood leftovers?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the same conversation between ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does offering a cup of disqualified blood turn the remaining blood into שירים?

steps.title: The cup follows the same rule as the unfit person
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the disqualified cup has the same law as the unfit person. Whatever you hold about the פסול, hold the same about the כוס פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What do you hold about an unfit person himself? If an unfit person creates leftovers, a disqualified cup also creates leftovers. If an unfit person does not create leftovers, a disqualified cup also does not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers by tying the new case to the case of the unfit person, saying the two have the same law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, רבי יוחנן does not give a separate ruling for the cup. He says it is no different from a service done by a פסול: both are flawed services, so they share one rule. The question about the cup is answered by the question about the person.

keyTerms.meaning: Itself; the person himself
What is your opinion?
Makes into; renders
Also

steps.whatToRemember: In רב זביד's version, a כוס פסול and a פסול person share the same rule about creating שירים. רבי יוחנן links the two cases instead of ruling on the cup separately.

phrases.english: He said to him:
About an unfit person himself, what do you hold?
If an unfit person renders the blood leftovers,
a disqualified cup also renders it leftovers.
If an unfit person does not render it leftovers,

phrases.aramaic: כּוֹס פָּסוּל נָמֵי לָא מְשַׁוֵּי שִׁירַיִם.
phrases.english: a disqualified cup also does not render it leftovers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of רב זביד's version by comparing it to the case of the unfit person.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The כוס פסול has the same law as the פסול person: if one creates שירים, so does the other, and if one does not, neither does the other.

steps.title: רב ירמיה's version: does one cup make the other cup rejected or leftover?
steps.stepSummary: In רב ירמיה מדיפתי's version, אביי asks רבה whether a cup used for the service makes the blood in the other cup דחוי or שירים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ירמיה מדיפתי teaches it this way: אביי asked רבה: If one cup was used, what happens to the other cup? Is it rejected, or is it leftover blood?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third version of the question from Steps 2 and 4. Now the question is about two valid cups: if the כהן used only one cup on the מזבח, what is the status of the other cup?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Steps 2 and 4 the question was about something פסול, an unfit person or an unfit cup. Here the question moves to a fully valid cup. If the other cup is דחוי, it is poured into the drain. If it counts as שירים, it is poured on the יסוד of the מזבח like normal leftover blood.

keyTerms.meaning: Teaches it this way (gives a different version of the discussion)
Rejected: blood that is pushed aside and does not count as leftover blood
Its fellow; here, the other cup

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the earlier versions. Here neither cup is פסול. Both cups hold good blood, and the only question is what the unused cup becomes.

phrases.english: Rav Yirmeya of Difti teaches it this way:
Abaye asked of Rabbah:
phrases.notes: Some versions say רבא, the name in round brackets, but the corrected wording in square brackets is רבה, אביי's teacher.

phrases.english: A cup, what is the law,
does it make its fellow cup
rejected, or a remainder?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third version of the question, now about two valid cups instead of a פסול.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When only one of several valid cups is used for the placements, is the blood in the other cup דחוי or שירים?

steps.title: רבה: this is a known dispute
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that this question is really a dispute between רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון and the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is a dispute between רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון and the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה does not answer with a single ruling. He says that the question was already argued about by earlier תנאים, and he is about to show the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Linking the question to an existing מחלוקת means there is no single clear answer. It depends on which opinion you follow. The next steps bring the ברייתא where this argument appears.

keyTerms.meaning: A dispute or argument
The Sages, the majority opinion

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: פְּלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן וְרַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: It is a dispute between Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon and the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question by pointing to a תנאים dispute.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The status of the other cup depends on the מחלוקת between רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון and the רבנן.

steps.title: The ברייתא sets up two פסוקים side by side
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא notes that one פסוק says 'its blood' and a later פסוק says 'all its blood'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: Above, the verse says, 'He shall pour its blood.' Below, the verse says, 'And he shall pour all its blood.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה starts bringing the ברייתא that shows the dispute. This step only sets up two פסוקים. The ברייתא will learn from each of them in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסוקים are about pouring out the leftover blood of a חטאת at the base of the מזבח. One adds the word 'all' (כל), and the other leaves it out. The ברייתא will use this difference to teach two different cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Above / below, meaning an earlier verse and a later verse
He shall pour out

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
Above it says:
"He shall pour its blood,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:25, about the חטאת of a נשיא.

phrases.english: below it says:
"And he shall pour all its blood."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:30, about the חטאת of a regular person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the ברייתא that supports רבה's claim that there is a dispute.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's statement that the question is a תנאים dispute
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that reads ויקרא 4:25 and 4:30 side by side

steps.title: Placements from all four cups: all the leftover blood goes to the base
steps.stepSummary: If the blood was collected in four cups and one placement came from each cup, all four cups are poured on the יסוד. The source is 'all its blood'.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that if a חטאת's blood was collected in four cups, and one placement was given from this cup and one from that cup, all of them are poured on the base? The verse says, 'And he shall pour all its blood.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains the second ('below') פסוק. It uses the word 'all' to teach a case where every cup was used for one placement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of the four cups was used for the service, so each cup's leftover counts as real שירים. The word 'all' tells us to pour every cup on the יסוד, not just one.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know?
A placement of blood on a corner of the מזבח
The base of the מזבח, where leftover blood is poured
The verse teaches

phrases.english: From where do we know regarding a sin offering
whose blood he collected in four cups,
and he gave one placement from this cup
and one placement from that cup,
phrases.notes: He means one placement from each of the four cups, one for each corner of the מזבח.

phrases.english: that all of them are poured onto the base?
The verse states: "And he shall pour all its blood."

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִן לְחַטָּאת שֶׁקִּיבֵּל דָּמָהּ בְּאַרְבָּעָה כּוֹסוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the 'all its blood' verse from Step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When each of the four cups gave a placement, the leftover blood of all of them goes to the יסוד.

steps.title: All four placements from one cup: only that cup goes to the base
steps.stepSummary: If all four placements came from one cup, only that cup is poured on the יסוד. The other cups are poured into the אמה (drain). The source is 'its blood'.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think that if he gave four placements from one cup, all the cups should be poured on the base. The verse says, 'its blood.' How so? That cup is poured on the base, and the others are poured into the drain.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains the first ('above') פסוק, the one without 'all', and finishes the opinion of the רבנן. In their view the unused cups are treated as rejected. This is only one side of the dispute רבה mentioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the word 'all', the פסוק limits pouring on the יסוד to the cup that was actually used. The unused cups never took part in the service, so they are not שירים and go to the drain like דחוי blood. This is the רבנן's position. The other side of the dispute that רבה mentioned comes in step 11.

keyTerms.meaning: One might have thought
How so? (how do the two verses fit together)
The water channel (drain) running through the עזרה

steps.whatToRemember: Cups used for a placement count as שירים and go to the יסוד. According to the רבנן, cups that were not used go to the אמה, which means they are treated as דחוי.

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל נָתַן אַרְבַּע מַתָּנוֹת מִכּוֹס אֶחָד,
phrases.english: One might have thought: if he gave four placements from one cup,
all of them should be poured onto the base?
The verse states: "And its blood."
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק from Step 8 that does not have the word 'all'.

phrases.english: How so?
That cup is poured onto the base,
phrases.notes: He means the one cup that was actually used for the placements.

phrases.english: and those others are poured into the drain.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל נָתַן אַרְבַּע מַתָּנוֹת מִכּוֹס אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the 'its blood' verse and contrasts it with the case in Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the רבנן, when all four placements come from one cup, only that cup goes to the יסוד. The unused cups go to the אמה as rejected blood.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: all four cups go to the base
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון rules that even if all four placements came from one cup, the blood in all four cups is poured on the יסוד, based on 'all its blood'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says: How do we know that if a חטאת's blood was collected in four cups and all four placements were made from one cup, the blood in every cup is poured on the יסוד? The פסוק says: 'And all its blood he shall pour.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the other opinion. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says that even the unused cups get poured on the יסוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן in step 10 said that only the cup that was used goes to the יסוד, and the others go into the אמה. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון disagrees and uses 'all its blood' to include every cup. This means he treats the unused cups as שירים (leftover blood), not as דחוי (rejected blood). That is exactly the side of אביי's question in step 6.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin offering
Placements of blood on the altar
The base of the altar, where leftover blood is poured
'The verse teaches', which introduces the source

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon says:
From where do we know, for a sin offering
whose blood he collected in four cups
and he placed all four placements from one cup,
that all of them are poured onto the base?
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means all four cups, including the three that were never used.

phrases.english: The verse says: "And all its blood he shall pour."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to the רבנן's ruling in step 10
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even when all placements came from one cup, every cup is poured on the יסוד, because the extra cups count as שירים.

steps.title: But another verse says only 'its blood'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: there is also a פסוק that says just 'its blood', which suggests that not all the blood goes to the יסוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written: 'And its blood he shall pour'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון with the other פסוק, the one the רבנן used in step 10 to limit which blood is poured on the יסוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'all its blood' includes every cup, then the word 'its blood' (without 'all') seems to limit it. The גמרא wants to know what רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון does with that limiting פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But it is written', which introduces a challenge from a פסוק

phrases.english: But it is written: "And its blood he shall pour"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source used in step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's ruling that every cup goes to the יסוד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק that says only 'its blood' seems to exclude some of the blood, which goes against including every cup.

steps.title: רב אשי: 'its blood' excludes the blood left in the neck
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that 'its blood' excludes only the blood that stayed in the animal's neck and was never collected in a vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: That פסוק comes to exclude the leftover blood that is in the animal's neck.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי defends רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. He says the limiting פסוק is talking about different blood altogether.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, 'its blood' does not exclude the unused cups. It excludes blood that never entered a vessel at all, the blood still in the animal's throat. So both פסוקים are explained: 'all its blood' includes every cup, and 'its blood' leaves out the neck blood.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude
The animal's neck or throat

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן say that unused cups go to the אמה, so those cups are דחוי. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says every cup goes to the יסוד, so the cups are שירים. In his view, only the blood left in the neck is excluded.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
That verse comes to exclude the leftover blood
that is in the animal's neck.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the limiting פסוק to a different case
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Its blood' excludes only the uncollected blood in the animal's neck, so all the cups still go to the יסוד.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: a fit priest handed the blood to an unfit person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of a fit כהן who collected the blood and handed it to an unfit person.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: If the fit one collected the blood and gave it to the unfit one, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic by quoting the משנה. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא explains why the משנה lists several similar cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught three cases where the blood is simply brought back: from an unfit person to a fit כהן, from the left hand to the right, and from a non-sacred vessel to a sacred one. The 'etc.' points to all of them.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit (for the Temple service)
Unfit
'Etc.', meaning the rest of the משנה continues

phrases.english: If the fit one collected and gave to the unfit one, etc.
phrases.notes: The rest of the משנה says to return it to the fit כהן. It adds the cases of the left hand and a non-sacred vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood that passed to an unfit person, the left hand, or a non-sacred vessel is brought back and used.

steps.title: Why the unfit-person case alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that all the cases are needed. From the unfit-person case alone, we might think it only means a טמא כהן, who is sometimes allowed to serve, and not the left hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was necessary to state all the cases. If the משנה had taught only 'unfit', I would have said: What does 'unfit' mean? A טמא כהן, who is fit for public service. But the left hand would not be fixable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a צריכותא, an explanation of why each case in the משנה is needed. This is the first part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טמא כהן is not totally unfit, because when the community is טמא he may bring public offerings. So we might think the blood is not ruined only because of his partial fitness. The left hand never counts for this service, so we might have thought it ruins the blood. That is why the משנה had to state the left-hand case too.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And it is necessary', which explains why each case had to be stated
'I would have said', the mistaken assumption
Ritually impure
Public (communal) Temple service
The left hand

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a dispute. The גמרא is only explaining why the משנה needed to list several cases that look the same.

phrases.english: And it was necessary;
for if it had taught us only 'unfit',
I would have said:
What is 'unfit'? An impure כהן,
who is fit for public service;
phrases.notes: When most of the people are impure, impure כהנים may bring the public offerings.

phrases.english: but the left hand, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the משנה in step 14 lists more than one case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The unfit-person case alone could be explained by a טמא כהן's partial fitness, so the left-hand case had to be stated separately.

steps.title: Why the left-hand case alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: From the left-hand case alone, we might think it works only because the left hand is valid on יום הכיפורים, and that a non-sacred vessel would not be fixable.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the משנה had taught only the left hand, I would have said that is because the left hand is valid on יום הכיפורים. But a non-sacred vessel would not be fixable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the צריכותא with the second part, showing why the left-hand case cannot replace the non-sacred-vessel case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום הכיפורים the כהן גדול carries the incense spoon in his left hand, so the left hand has some validity in the Temple service. A non-sacred vessel has no such validity anywhere, so we might think it ruins the blood. That is why the משנה needed the vessel case as well.

keyTerms.meaning: A situation where it is valid
The Day of Atonement
Non-sacred (ordinary) vessels

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only the left hand,
I would say that is because it is valid on Yom Kippur;
phrases.notes: On יום הכיפורים the כהן גדול carries the incense spoon in his left hand.

phrases.english: but non-sacred vessels, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the צריכותא from step 15
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The left-hand case alone could be explained by its validity on יום הכיפורים, so the non-sacred-vessel case had to be stated separately.

steps.title: The non-sacred vessel case alone would not teach the others, so all are needed
steps.stepSummary: From the כלי חול case alone, we might think it is fixable only because such vessels can be made holy. So the משנה needs all three cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the משנה had taught us only the non-sacred vessel, we might say it works because those vessels can be made holy. But these others (an unfit person, the left hand) can never become fit, so I would say they are not fixable. That is why all the cases are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the last piece of its 'why do we need every case' explanation and then concludes: all the cases are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כלי חול can be made into a holy vessel, so its problem is only temporary. An unfit person and a left hand have no such option, so we might have thought blood that reached them is lost. Since each case has its own special reason, none of them teaches the others.

keyTerms.meaning: Non-sacred vessels, not made holy for Temple use
To make them holy (consecrate them)
It is necessary, meaning each case teaches something the others cannot

steps.whatToRemember: Each of the three cases has its own possible reason for being fixable, so the משנה must spell out all of them.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only a non-sacred vessel,
that is because they are fit to be made holy;
but these, I would say not.
phrases.notes: 'These' means the unfit person and the left hand from the earlier cases.

phrases.english: It is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the three-part צריכותא begun in steps 15 and 16
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All three cases in the משנה are needed, because each has its own reason that could make it uniquely fixable.

steps.title: Shouldn't the blood become permanently rejected?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ruling itself: once the blood reached an unfit person, a left hand, or a כלי חול, it should be דחוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let the blood be considered rejected!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now questions the משנה's actual ruling. If the blood was in an invalid place for even a moment, why isn't it rejected forever?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known idea of דחוי: once a קרבן becomes unfit, it can stay rejected even after the problem goes away. The challenge says this blood should fall under that rule, so returning it to a fit כהן should not help.

keyTerms.meaning: Rejected; a קרבן that became unfit and stays unfit even after the problem is fixed
But let it be

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether the unfit person can do the עבודה. Everyone agrees he cannot. The question is whether the blood is ruined forever just because it passed through him.

phrases.english: But let it be rejected!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining why each case is listed to challenging the ruling itself
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the blood can be returned to a fit כהן and still be used
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Blood that was in an invalid state should be permanently rejected under the rule of דחוי

steps.title: The משנה follows חנן המצרי, who does not hold of rejection
steps.stepSummary: רבינא tells רב אשי, in the name of רבא, that the משנה follows חנן המצרי, who holds there is no דחוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: This is what רב ירמיה of דיפתי said in the name of רבא: Whose view is this משנה? It is חנן המצרי, who does not hold of rejection.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the challenge by saying the משנה follows a תנא who does not accept the rule of דחוי at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed everyone holds of דחוי. This answer says no: חנן המצרי holds that something that became unfit for a while is not rejected forever. Following him, the blood can be fixed and used.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this? A way to identify which תנא a ruling follows
חנן the Egyptian, a תנא
Who does not hold of the rule of rejection

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi,
So said Rav Yirmeya of Difti
in the name of Rava:
Whose view is this?
It is Chanan the Egyptian,
who does not hold of rejection.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 18
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the משנה to a specific תנא who rejects the premise of the question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone holds of דחוי, so the blood should be rejected
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows חנן המצרי, who holds there is no דחוי, so the blood can be fixed

steps.title: A ברייתא showing that חנן המצרי does not hold of rejection
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where חנן המצרי says that even when the blood is already in the cup, a new partner animal can be brought and paired.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: חנן המצרי says: Even if the blood is already in the cup, he brings its partner and pairs it with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that חנן המצרי really holds there is no דחוי, by quoting his words from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is about a pair of animals where one was lost after the other's blood was collected. One would think the collected blood is rejected, since it has no partner. חנן המצרי says a new partner can be brought, so the blood is not rejected, which shows he does not hold of דחוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Cup, the vessel holding the collected blood
Pairs, matches up

phrases.english: As it was taught: Chanan the Egyptian says:
Even if the blood is in the cup,
phrases.notes: This is about the two goats of יום הכיפורים, when the goat sent away is lost after the other one's blood was collected.

phrases.english: he brings its partner and pairs it with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the claim in step 19 about חנן המצרי
steps.raayaObject: That חנן המצרי does not hold of דחוי
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where חנן המצרי allows pairing a new partner even after the blood is in the cup

steps.title: Anything a person can fix himself is not rejected
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a different answer: if the problem is in his own power to fix, it is not דחוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Anything that is in his hand to fix is not considered rejected.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question about דחוי in a different way, so the משנה can fit even those who do hold of דחוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי agrees that דחוי exists in general. But here the כהן can simply take the blood back from the unfit person, the left hand, or the כלי חול. Since the fix is right in his hands, the blood never counts as truly rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: Anything that is in his hand, meaning in his power to fix
Is not considered rejected

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers: according to רבא (as reported by רבינא), the משנה follows חנן המצרי, who has no דחוי at all. According to רב אשי, even those who hold of דחוי agree that a problem you can fix yourself does not cause rejection.
steps.whyThisMatters: רב אשי's rule limits דחוי to problems a person cannot fix himself, so the משנה does not have to follow a single minority view.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Anything that is in his hand
phrases.notes: He means anything the person can fix by himself, like taking the blood back.

phrases.english: is not rejected.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר כֹּל שֶׁבְּיָדוֹ לָא הָוֵי דָּחוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the קשיא of step 18, different from רבינא's answer in step 19
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the rule of דחוי so that it does not apply to these cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Blood that was in an invalid state is rejected under the rule of דחוי
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the כהן can fix the problem himself, the blood is not rejected, even for those who hold of דחוי

steps.title: רב שייא says רב אשי's answer is more reasonable
steps.stepSummary: רב שייא sides with רב אשי, pointing out that the תנא known to hold of דחוי is רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שייא said: It makes more sense to follow רב אשי. Who is the one we know holds of rejection? רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שייא says that רב אשי's answer, 'what is in his power to fix is not דחוי', is better than saying the משנה follows חנן המצרי. He starts by naming the תנא who holds of דחוי: רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that we do not need to push the משנה onto the lone opinion of חנן המצרי. If even רבי יהודה, who holds of דחוי, agrees with רב אשי's rule, then the משנה fits everyone. The next steps bring the proofs.

keyTerms.meaning: like him, in line with his view
it makes sense, it is reasonable
the idea of rejection: once disqualified, it stays disqualified

phrases.english: Rav Shaya said:
It is reasonable to follow Rav Ashi.
Whom have you heard
who holds of rejection? Rabbi Yehuda;

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שַׁיָּיא: כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרַב אָשֵׁי מִסְתַּבְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Chooses רב אשי's answer (step 21) over רבינא's חנן המצרי answer (step 19).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אשי's approach is more reasonable; the תנא who holds of דחוי is רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Proof that רבי יהודה holds of rejection: the goats of יום הכיפורים
steps.stepSummary: A משנה in יומא shows רבי יהודה holds that if one of the יום הכיפורים goats is lost, the other goat is permanently rejected.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: And furthermore רבי יהודה said: If the blood spilled, the scapegoat is left to die. If the scapegoat died, the blood is spilled out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that רבי יהודה holds of דחוי. In his view, if one of the two goats of יום הכיפורים is lost, the other cannot be used and a new pair is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two goats were set aside as a pair. Once one side of the pair fails, רבי יהודה says the remaining one is pushed off for good. That is clear דחוי.

keyTerms.meaning: the goat sent away on יום הכיפורים (the scapegoat)
spilled

phrases.english: as we learned: And furthermore Rabbi Yehuda said:
If the blood spilled, the scapegoat must die;
phrases.notes: 'The blood' means the blood of the goat offered to ה׳, spilled before it was sprinkled.

phrases.english: if the scapegoat died, the blood must be spilled out;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim in step 22 that רבי יהודה holds of דחוי.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה holds of דחוי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in יומא about the two Yom Kippur goats.

steps.title: Yet רבי יהודה says what is in one's power to fix is not rejected
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה lets a כהן fill a cup from blood mixed on the floor and sprinkle it. So something fixable is not דחוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we have heard him say: anything in his power to fix is not rejected. As it is taught: רבי יהודה says: The כהן would fill one cup from the mixed blood and throw it with one throwing against the base of the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the same רבי יהודה also holds רב אשי's rule. Blood that spilled can still be gathered up and used, because fixing it is in the כהן's hands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blood had spilled out of its cup, which might seem to push it off. Still, רבי יהודה lets the כהן scoop it up and sprinkle it. This means spilling is not דחוי when the כהן himself can fix the problem.

keyTerms.meaning: anything that is in his power (to fix)
the mixed blood (of many offerings, gathered from the floor)
the base of the מזבח
throwing or sprinkling the blood on the מזבח

phrases.english: And we have heard him say:
Anything in his power to fix is not rejected.
As it is taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: כּוֹס אֶחָד הָיָה מְמַלֵּא מִדַּם הַתַּעֲרוֹבֶת,
phrases.english: He would fill one cup from the mixed blood,
phrases.notes: This is the blood of the many פסח offerings that spilled and mixed together on the floor.

phrases.english: and throw it with one throwing against the base.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשָׁמְעִינַן לֵיהּ דְּאָמַר: כֹּל שֶׁבְּיָדוֹ לָא הָוֵי דָּחוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the same רבי יהודה from step 23 limits דחוי to cases outside one's control.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה holds כל שבידו לא הוי דחוי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא about filling one cup from the mixed blood of the פסח offerings.

steps.title: Conclusion: anything in one's power to fix is not rejected
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws the lesson from רבי יהודה's ברייתא and confirms it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from it: anything in his power to fix is not rejected! Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the lesson of the ברייתא and agrees with it. Even רבי יהודה says that a problem the כהן can fix does not cause דחוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This finishes רב שייא's argument. רבי יהודה holds of דחוי and also holds רב אשי's rule. So our משנה can follow רבי יהודה, and we do not need to say it follows only חנן המצרי.

keyTerms.meaning: learn from it; as a reply, 'yes, that is the lesson'

steps.whatToRemember: Even the תנא who holds of דחוי (רבי יהודה) agrees that something the person can fix himself is not דחוי. That is why רב אשי's answer is the more reasonable one.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: כֹּל שֶׁבְּיָדוֹ – לָא הָוֵי דָּחוּי!
phrases.english: Learn from it: anything in his power to fix is not rejected!
Learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: כֹּל שֶׁבְּיָדוֹ לָא הָוֵי דָּחוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws and confirms the inference from the ברייתא in step 24.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: כל שבידו לא הוי דחוי, even according to רבי יהודה, which supports רב אשי.

steps.title: The full ברייתא: why fill one cup from the mixed blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה's ברייתא in full. The cup of mixed blood is filled so that if one offering's blood spilled, this sprinkling makes that offering valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: It is taught, רבי יהודה says: The כהן would fill one cup from the mixed blood, so that if the blood of one of them had spilled, it turns out that this sprinkling makes it valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to study the ברייתא itself and gives its full wording, including רבי יהודה's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Among all the פסח offerings, maybe one offering's cup of blood spilled before it was sprinkled. Some of that offering's blood is likely in the mixture on the floor. So sprinkling one cup of the mixture covers it and makes that offering valid.

keyTerms.meaning: 'the matter itself': the גמרא now studies a source it quoted earlier
makes it valid

phrases.english: The matter itself: It is taught, Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: כּוֹס אֶחָד הָיָה מְמַלֵּא מִדַּם הַתַּעֲרוֹבֶת,
phrases.english: He would fill one cup from the mixed blood,
so that if one of them spilled,
phrases.notes: 'One of them' means the cup of blood from one of the פסח offerings.

phrases.english: it turns out that this makes it valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא quoted in step 24 to study it in full.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sprinkling one cup of mixed blood validates any offering whose own blood spilled.

steps.title: The חכמים object: the mixed blood was not received in a vessel
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים challenge רבי יהודה: the blood on the floor was not received in a כלי, so it should not be fit to sprinkle.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to רבי יהודה: But it was not received in a vessel!
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים attack רבי יהודה's ruling. Blood must be received in a כלי, and blood that flowed straight onto the floor was never received.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that receiving the blood in a vessel (קבלה) is a required step. Blood that never went into a vessel cannot be sprinkled, so how can the mixture make the offering valid?

keyTerms.meaning: was received (collected) in a vessel
but surely, isn't it so that

phrases.english: They said to Rabbi Yehuda:
But it was not received in a vessel!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה: וַהֲלֹא לֹא נִתְקַבֵּל בִּכְלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יהודה's ruling from step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's ruling that the cup of mixed blood validates the offering.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Blood must be received in a כלי, and the blood on the floor may never have been.

steps.title: How could the חכמים know that?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the חכמים could be sure the blood was never received in a vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do they know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the wording of the חכמים' objection. Nobody can know for certain that this blood was not received in a vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe the blood was received in a cup and then spilled. If so, it was properly received. So a flat statement that 'it was not received' does not make sense.

keyTerms.meaning: how do they know?

phrases.english: How do they know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how certain the objection in step 27 can be.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the חכמים could know the blood was never received in a vessel.

steps.title: Rather, the חכמים meant: perhaps it was not received in a vessel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the objection as a doubt: maybe this blood was never received in a vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they meant: perhaps it was not received in a vessel!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the reading of the חכמים' objection. They did not mean it was certainly not received, only that it might not have been.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a doubt is enough for the objection. The mixture might be blood that flowed straight from the animal to the floor, which was never fit to sprinkle. So the cup might not truly make the offering valid.

keyTerms.meaning: perhaps, maybe

phrases.english: Rather: perhaps it was not received in a vessel!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 28 by turning the חכמים' certain claim into a doubt.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The objection means 'perhaps it was not received in a vessel.'

steps.title: רבי יהודה begins his answer
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה starts to reply to the חכמים; his answer comes in the next lines.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them:
steps.whatsHappening: This short line sets up the next move. רבי יהודה is about to answer the חכמים' doubt, and his words come right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים' worry, that the blood may never have been received in a vessel, has not been answered yet on this amud. רבי יהודה's answer to that doubt comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: he said to them

phrases.english: He said to them:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens רבי יהודה's reply to the objection in steps 27–29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Setup line; the actual answer follows in the next lines.
